title: Brewers RHP Jacob Misiorowski breaks own MLB record with 105.5 mph pitch
content:
Milwaukee Brewers right-hander Jacob Misiorowski threw the fastest pitch by a starting pitcher since MLB began tracking such things in 2008.

Have you heard this story before?

On his third pitch Friday, the 6-foot-7 flamethrower uncorked a 105.5 mph fastball that Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong actually managed to foul off. It was a statement of intent in the first game of a three-game series in Milwaukee.

Misiorowski held the Cubs hitless before Seiya Suzuki homered leading off the fifth inning, and eventually exited after six innings with eight strikeouts, four walks, two hits and one earned run on 107 pitches (69 strikes). The Brewers won the game 6-2, as Misiorowski moved to 9-3 on the season.

Misiorowski’s heater at the top of the night broke his own record of 104.5 mph, set two starts prior against the Philadelphia Phillies on June 12. In his last start, on June 19, he threw a 104.2 mph fastball, good for third among starters since MLB began tracking velocity in 2008. Friday’s record-setting pitch against the Cubs was his seventh 104-plus mph pitch in his past three starts.

“My observation of him is, I thought he had the best arm I’ve seen in baseball since I don’t know since when,” MLB Hall of Famer Nolan Ryan told The Athletic’s Jayson Stark in a recent interview Stark did with MLB’s all-time career strikeout leader. “I really think he has a gift there.”

So, “The Miz” broke his own velocity record, which itself had broken his own record before that.

And before that.

In fact, if you go look at the top 51 fastest clocked pitches by a starter since such figures have been tracked, you’ll have to peruse down to No. 35 to find any name other than Misiorowski (once Friday’s heat was entered into the ranks). That would be Jordan Hicks, who threw a 103.2 mph pitch as a member of the St. Louis Cardinals in a 7-6 win over the Los Angeles Dodgers on July 12, 2022.

Keep going down the list, and it’s more Misiorowski, and then Hicks again at No. 40. Then a whole bunch more Misiorowski heat. Of the 51 fastest pitches recorded by a starter, the 24-year-old Brewers ace has thrown 49 of them.

Factor in relievers, however, and Misiorowski takes a back seat (for now) to well-traveled left-hander Aroldis Chapman, who uncorked a 105.8 mph heater in 2024 while he was a member of the Cincinnati Reds. Chapman also has a 105.7 mph pitch on the books while with the Yankees in 2018. Angels right-hander Ben Joyce and Misiorowski are tied at No. 3 on the all-time list at 105.5.

“To look at my career, and the point where (Misiorowski) is in his career today, he’s much further down the road now than I was,” Ryan told Stark.

It’s just another shining step on a blistering start to the season for Misiorowski. In his second year in the majors, he’s leading the big leagues in ERA (1.45) and strikeouts.

His heat has helped the Brewers to a 50-29 record, good for a 7 1/2 game lead atop the National League Central and for second in the NL behind the two-time reigning champion Los Angeles Dodgers (52-29).

Misiorowski has drawn comparisons to a young Ryan, one that “The Ryan Express” rejects, telling Stark, “Would I compare myself to him? No, I wouldn’t.”
